summary: Checks whether a value is **not** a domain name.
description: `nonValidDomain(value)` is the same test as `!isValidDomain(value)`, written so that a guard clause reads as a sentence rather than as a negation.
Labels separated by single dots, with no leading or trailing dot or hyphen and no empty label. It is a syntax check: whether the domain resolves is another question.
`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).
returns: `true` when the value is not a domain name; otherwise `false`.

examples.title: What passes and what does not
examples.body:
```javascript
nonValidDomain("-example.com"); // => true
nonValidDomain("example..com"); // => true
nonValidDomain("example.com."); // => true
nonValidDomain(""); // => true
nonValidDomain("example.com"); // => false
nonValidDomain("sub.example.co.uk"); // => false
```
